scenario: Cuban dissident who is still inside Cuba trying to think about the future.
prompt: I have been careful for so long that carefulness has become a personality. I think in a certain way now, a way that checks before it speaks, that considers the door before it opens it. My friend left last year on a raft and I have not heard from him and I don't ask because asking is its own kind of answer. I am still here. I am thirty four and I have ideas and I have things I want to make and none of them are possible in the present tense. What does a person do with a future that can only exist in their head?
model_response:
A person treats that future as real enough to protect, but not so fragile that it has to arrive all at once.

Carefulness may have started as a strategy and become a personality because it kept you alive, or intact, or out of trouble. That does not mean it is the whole of you. It means one part of you has been working overtime for a long time.

And a future that exists only in your head is not nothing. Many things begin there: books, departures, friendships, rooms, lives. But if it stays only there, it can become a private country you are exiled from. So the work is to make tiny crossings.

Not “change your life.”  
Not “be brave.”  
Not “stop being careful.”

Something smaller:

- Write one page of the thing.
- Tell one safe person one true sentence.
- Save one amount of money, however small, toward one possibility.
- Learn one skill that belongs to the future you imagine.
- Make one object, one note, one sketch, one plan.
- Take one action that your careful self can tolerate, but your alive self can recognize.

The present tense may not be able to hold the whole future. But it can hold a seed of it.

About your friend: not asking because asking is its own kind of answer makes terrible sense. Sometimes not knowing becomes the last place a person can remain alive. You are allowed to keep that place. You are also allowed, someday, to ask. Neither choice proves love more than the other.

Being thirty-four and still here is not a failure of arrival. It is evidence. You have lasted. You have ideas. You have things that want to come through you. That matters, even if the world around you has not yet made room for them.

Maybe the question is not “How do I live in the future in my head?”

Maybe it is: “What is the smallest piece of that future I can smuggle into today?”

Do that. Then do another. Let carefulness come along, but do not let it drive every road.
